workflow.name: UP-wi-mall-vectoriser
workflow.description: Turns jovi-mall product payloads into searchable rows: builds the product prose with code (no AI), embeds it with Voyage voyage-4, and stores it in the Postgres product_vectors hybrid-search table. Accepts one product, an array, or a CSV/Excel sheet; answ

parameters.responseBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ success: true, job_id: $execution.id, accepted: $('accept job').all().filter(i => i.json.accepted).map(i => i.json.product_id), rejected: $('accept job').all().filter(i => !i.json.accepted).map(i => ({ product_id: i.json.product_id, reason: i.json.reason })), callback_url: $('accept job').first().json.callback_url }) }}

parameters.query: UPDATE product_vectors SET metadata = jsonb_set(metadata, '{status}', to_jsonb($2::text), true) WHERE metadata->>'product_id' = $1 RETURNING product_id, status
DELETE FROM product_vectors WHERE metadata->>'product_id' = $1 RETURNING product_id

parameters.content:
## The contract, and who holds which half

jovi-mall `VectorisationService` calls three paths off `VECTORISER_BASE_URL`:

- `POST <base>` — one payload object, an array of them, or `{products:[...]}`
- `POST <base>/status` — `{product_id, vectorised_id, new_status}`
- `POST <base>/delete` — `{product_id, vectorised_id}`

All three are live, so jovi-mall's `.env` must carry
`VECTORISER_BASE_URL=https://the8n.wi-mall.com/webhook/vectorise`.

### ⛔ THE HOST MOVED — and this half cannot be fixed from n8n

It was `the8n.fante.cloud`, which now answers **`404 page not found`** (measured
2026-09-13). Every other base URL in these workflows is read from n8n's OWN
environment, so it is fixed here. **This one is not**: `VECTORISER_BASE_URL` lives in
**jovi-mall's** environment, so until jovi-mall is updated and redeployed every
vectorisation request posts into a dead host — and `VectorisationService` retries
three times before giving up, so the symptom is slow, not loud.

### ⛔ The four webhooks are still on the WRONG credential

They were auto-assigned **`whatsapp_auth`**, whose header is `Authorization`.
jovi-mall sends **`VECTORISER_API_KEY`**, so every real call 403s until this is
fixed. It fails closed, which is the right direction, but it does not work yet.

**Do not edit `whatsapp_auth`** — WhatsApp uses it. Create a NEW Header Auth
credential with Name `VECTORISER_API_KEY` and Value
`={{ $env.VECTORISER_API_KEY }}` (the leading `=` makes it an expression, which
resolves because the container sets `N8N_BLOCK_ENV_ACCESS_IN_NODE=false`), then
select it on `vectorise`, `vectorise file`, `status change` and `delete request`.

### The 202

`POST <base>` answers **202 immediately** and reports per product later. The
caller must treat the 202 body's `accepted` list as "now pending" and its
`rejected` list as "failed, do not wait for these".

## Why no model builds this text

Re-indexing must be **idempotent**: the same product has to produce the same
vector, or an unrelated price edit reshuffles everyone's search results. A model
also invents attributes no vendor typed, and the agent quotes them as fact.

The sentence still changes with the product **type** and with which fields the
vendor actually filled in — a service is priced per minute, a download is never
"out of stock", a physical variant carries weight and dimensions. That is
branching, not generation.

⚠ The **bargain window numbers never enter the text.** `minPrice` is the selling
price and `maxPrice` is the ceiling haggling may reach — that is the negotiating
agent's hand, and the text is read straight into a customer-facing model's
context. `bargainable: true` says the door is open; the numbers stay in
`metadata.bargain_windows` for a server-side caller only.

## Delete, insert, then overwrite the metadata

Three steps rather than one, and each is load-bearing:

1. **purge** — the PGVector node only ever INSERTs. Without the delete, every
   re-index adds a second row and the same product appears twice in a five-item
   chat list, half of it at a stale price. `product_vectors` also has a UNIQUE
   index on `product_id`, so a missed purge fails loudly instead of duplicating.
2. **embed and store** — the loader passes ONE metadata key, `product_id`,
   because n8n metadata values are strings and the real object has arrays and
   numbers in it.
3. **write the searchable metadata** — replaces that jsonb with the full object.
   Every generated column in `product_vectors` (`price_min`, `in_stock`,
   `status`, `tsv`, …) is derived from it, so this is the step that makes the
   row findable at all.

`alwaysOutputData` on both Postgres nodes is deliberate: a DELETE matching
nothing must not stop the chain. It is safe here **only because** everything
downstream reads `$('build product text')` explicitly and never `$json`.

## One CHUNK per iteration, not one product

The loop used to run one product at a time, calling Voyage once each. That hit a
wall: this account's free tier is **3 requests per minute** without a payment
method, so the fourth product of any minute was refused — and, worse, reported as
succeeded.

Now `build all texts` builds every product's prose in one pass and groups them
into chunks of **32**, and each iteration makes **one** embedding request and
**one** upsert.

⚠ 32 rather than Voyage's maximum of 128 because requests stop being the binding
limit once you batch — **tokens** do. 10K per minute on the free tier, at roughly
150–300 tokens a product, is about 40 products a minute whatever the chunk size.
A 128-product chunk could not fit in one minute's budget, so it could not be
retried into success either; it would just fail bigger.

**The verdict comes from `RETURNING product_id`, never from a node saying it
succeeded.** That rule is not decoration — see the note on `chunk outcome`.

## Status and delete never re-embed

The product **status is not in the embedded text** — it is a filter column
derived from `metadata`. So archiving a product is one `jsonb_set`, with no
Voyage call and no new vector. That is the whole reason to keep it out of the
prose.

Both answer synchronously; the caller only needs a 2xx.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ input: $json.products.map(p => p.text), model: 'voyage-4', input_type: 'document', output_dimension: 1024, output_dtype: 'float', truncation: true }) }}

parameters.query:
INSERT INTO product_vectors (text, metadata, embedding)
SELECT x.txt, x.meta, x.emb::vector
FROM jsonb_to_recordset($1::jsonb) AS x(txt text, meta jsonb, emb text)
ON CONFLICT (product_id) DO UPDATE
   SET text = EXCLUDED.text,
       metadata = EXCLUDED.metadata,
       embedding = EXCLUDED.embedding,
       indexed_at = now()
RETURNING product_id
